name: Mid-Century Walnut Console TV
descriptions: Floor-standing wooden cabinet in walnut veneer with integrated speaker grilles and tapered legs — a living-room centerpiece.
Houses a compact CRT behind a fabric screen and a single dial tuner; designed to look like furniture rather than electronics.
Heavy and static by design; restore the finish and it blends with vintage modern interiors.

name: 1970s Wood-Panel Entertainment Console
descriptions: Wide low cabinet with wood-grain laminate, sliding glass doors and room for a record player, radio, and TV set.
Built-in shelving and cable passthroughs for VHS players and stereo components; evokes retro family dens.
Large footprint and weight make it a fixed statement piece for period-style rooms.

name: 1980s VHS Entertainment Center
descriptions: Laminate TV stand with a dedicated VCR shelf, headphone jack, and decorative chrome accents.
Designed to hold a boxy CRT up to 32 inches, multiple VHS tapes and a handful of VHS boxes behind glass doors.
Practical and era-accurate for a retro-media themed room; sturdy but not meant to be moved often.

name: Roll-Top CRT TV Cart (1990s)
descriptions: Mobile metal and wood cart with casters, a strap to secure a CRT, and lower shelves for consoles and tapes.
Common in dorms and family rooms before flat-screens — allows the bulky television to be repositioned easily.
Casters lock for stability; not intended for stacking other heavy items on top.

name: Early-2000s Glass-Shelf Entertainment Unit
descriptions: Contemporary unit with tempered glass shelves, brushed metal supports and a flat-panel LCD mount.
Designed to organize DVD players, cable boxes and a modest surround-sound receiver while keeping a sleek profile.
A neutral transitional piece that suits early-plasma/LED flat screens and physical media collections.

name: Wall-Mounted Modern OLED TV
descriptions: Ultra-thin smart display with near-bezel-less glass and an almost flush wall-mount for a gallery look.
Integrated smart platform and voice controls, HDMI eARC, and a slim soundbar option; minimalist aesthetic.
Installed as a permanent fixture — treated like architectural furniture in contemporary interiors.

name: Home Theater Projector with Retractable Screen
descriptions: Ceiling- or shelf-mounted projector paired with a motorized retractable screen — cinema vibes at home.
Projector sits on a shelf or mount (portable unit), while the screen is a fixed installation that reads as furniture.
Ideal for dark rooms and movie nights; requires a stable place for the projector and wiring access for power/source.

name: Upright Arcade Cabinet
descriptions: Full-size arcade machine with joystick and button controls, CRT or modern monitor, marquee lighting and coin door aesthetics.
Heavy and stand-alone — functions as both furniture and a playable entertainment system in game rooms or lounges.
Power and wiring required; a nostalgic focal point that can't be stacked or easily moved.

name: Hi‑Fi Turntable Stereo Console
descriptions: Cabinet-style stereo with built-in turntable, AM/FM tuner, and large wooden speaker enclosures.
Designed for vinyl enthusiasts who want the equipment integrated into furniture rather than exposed racks.
A tactile, warm-sounding centerpiece — heavy and intentionally stationary.

name: Vintage Home Game Console (Cartridge)
descriptions: Compact retro console with cartridge slot and simple A/V outputs — a grab-and-play piece of gaming history.
Portable enough to place on shelves or TV stands; pairs naturally with the retro TVs in this bundle.
Electronic and collectible rather than furniture; small, non-stackable, and best kept with its controllers.

name: Mid-Century Console TV
descriptions: A low wooden console TV set with tapered legs and warm walnut veneer, evoking 1950s living rooms.
Glass screen set into a modestly curved bezel, with a fabric speaker grille and rotary dials on the side.
Fits as a statement furniture piece in retro-modern interiors; ideal for a cozy, nostalgic vibe.

name: Art Deco Salon Television
descriptions: An elegant Art Deco-era TV with geometric brass inlays, lacquered black panels, and stepped silhouettes.
The screen sits within a decorative metal frame; ornate knobs and a small shelf for magazines complete the look.
Adds glamour and period charm to formal parlors or galleries with vintage-inspired decor.

name: Minimalist Wall-Mounted OLED
descriptions: A super-thin, wall-mounted OLED display with an ultra-fine bezel and matte black finish.
Designed for contemporary spaces that favor clean lines and unobtrusive technology.
Blends into the wall when off; works well in modern, Scandinavian, or minimalist interiors.

name: Futuristic Holographic Console
descriptions: A conceptual furniture piece hosting a suspended holographic display within a pedestal console.
Polished surfaces and soft LED accents give it a sci-fi, forward-looking aesthetic.
Serves as a centerpiece for high-tech or avant-garde living spaces where art and display merge.

name: Wooden Retro CRT TV with Fabric Speaker
descriptions: A chunky cathode-ray TV housed in a reclaimed oak cabinet with a woven fabric speaker panel.
Rounded CRT screen, classic dials, and a scent of old wood give it an authentic retro character.
Perfect for vintage-themed rooms, record-listening corners, or as a nostalgic prop.

name: Industrial Metal Frame Television
descriptions: A rugged television encased in a raw steel frame with visible rivets and a weathered patina.
Exposed hardware, pipe-like supports, and a utilitarian control panel suit lofts and workshop aesthetics.
Brings an urban, factory-inspired vibe to industrial and eclectic interiors.

name: Boho Upcycled TV Cabinet
descriptions: A lovingly refurbished TV cabinet made from mixed woods, woven cane panels, and colorful hand-painted motifs.
Soft, mismatched finishes and tactile materials lend a relaxed, artisan bohemian energy.
Works well in creative studios, sunrooms, or laid-back communal spaces that celebrate craft.

name: Steampunk Brass Tube Television
descriptions: A decorative TV with brass fittings, exposed vacuum-tube accents, and filigree castings for a steampunk aesthetic.
The display is housed behind a smoked glass bezel; mechanical switches and pressure gauges add theatrical detail.
A theatrical conversation piece for themed rooms or collectors of speculative historical design.

name: Japanese Low-Profile Chabudai TV Stand
descriptions: A low-slung TV console inspired by traditional Japanese minimalism, crafted from light maple with subtle joinery.
Designed to sit close to the floor, it complements tatami rooms or modern interiors seeking calm simplicity.
Its compact footprint makes it suitable for tight urban apartments and serene, uncluttered spaces.

name: 1980s Neon Accent TV
descriptions: A bold, boxy television with glossy plastic panels, neon trim, and an unmistakable retro-80s colorway.
Angular design and chrome details make it a playful throwback for nostalgia-driven interiors or game rooms.
Pairs well with vintage arcade machines and vibrant, maximalist decor.

name: Victorian Parlor Ornate Television
descriptions: An ornate television cabinet influenced by Victorian parlor furniture, with carved flourishes and dark polish.
The screen is framed by decorative moldings and gold leaf accents, blending antique formality with modern function.
Ideal for eclectic interiors that juxtapose historical opulence with contemporary technology.

name: Portable Suitcase TV
descriptions: A compact, suitcase-style portable television with a leather handle, fold-down legs, and a protective latch.
Design nods to mid-century travel gear and early portable electronics; practical and charming in small spaces.
Useful as a movable display or decorative prop in vintage-travel themed rooms.

name: Mid-Century Console TV
descriptions: Low wooden console with tapered legs and integrated speaker grille, inspired by 1950s design.
Warm walnut finish, open shelf for a record player or VHS player, and a recessed space for a CRT or a small flatscreen.
Balances vintage charm with practical storage; fits well in retro or eclectic living rooms.

name: Retro CRT Television
descriptions: Boxy cathode-ray tube television with rounded glass screen and wood-paneled casing.
Large dial knobs and a fabric speaker face give an authentic late-1970s living-room feel.
Heavy and solid; ideal as a nostalgic focal point in a themed room or as a prop.

name: Modern Wall-Mounted Smart TV
descriptions: Slim, bezel-minimal flat screen designed for wall mounting with hidden cable channel.
Supports streaming apps and has a low-profile soundbar shelf beneath the screen.
Clean, contemporary aesthetic suited to minimalist or tech-forward interiors.

name: Art Deco Television Cabinet
descriptions: Stylized cabinet with geometric inlays, lacquered finish, and brass accents reflecting 1930s glamour.
Conceals modern electronics behind decorative doors and has a mirrored back panel to accentuate the screen.
Makes the TV feel like fine furniture — works well in formal or theatrical interiors.

name: Minimalist Floating Media Shelf
descriptions: Wall-attached floating shelf designed to hold a slim TV and a couple of media devices with hidden mounting points.
Matte finish, clean lines, and integrated cable channel for an uncluttered look.
Perfect for small apartments or Scandinavian-inspired spaces where simplicity is key.

name: Rustic Farmhouse Entertainment Console
descriptions: Chunky plank-style console in distressed pine with open shelving and a couple of sliding barn doors.
Provides roomy storage for consoles, media boxes, and baskets; tactile, weathered finish for cozy spaces.
Pairs well with natural textiles and vintage decor.

name: Industrial Metal TV Stand with Speakers
descriptions: Sturdy steel frame with reclaimed wood shelves and integrated speaker mounts for a loft-style setup.
Open shelving encourages visible, organized cables and a workshop-inspired aesthetic.
Durable, utilitarian design that pairs with exposed brick or concrete finishes.

name: Victorian Mahogany TV Armoire
descriptions: Tall mahogany armoire with carved details and hinged doors that close to hide electronics.
Interior shelving and ventilation panels allow storage of a medium-sized TV and media components.
Adds formality and antique character to traditional interiors while keeping tech out of sight.

name: Bohemian Woven Media Cabinet
descriptions: Low cabinet with rattan-fronted doors, eclectic hardware, and a sun-faded painted finish.
Light, airy look that blends artisan craft with functionality — good for relaxed, layered interiors.
Offers concealed storage for media while adding texture and warmth to the room.

name: Scandinavian Oak Media Unit
descriptions: Slim-profile oak unit with a combination of drawers and open cubbies, light natural finish, and subtle tapering.
Designed for functionality and understated beauty; integrates cable cutouts and ventilation.
Versatile classic that suits modern, minimalist, and Nordic-inspired interiors.

name: Classic CRT Television
descriptions: Boxy cathode-ray TV with curved glass screen and wood-veneered casing.
Front panel includes dials for channel and volume plus a pair of rabbit-ear antennae.
Heavier and deeper than modern sets; fits well in retro or classic living-room setups.

name: Mid-century Entertainment Console
descriptions: Low, long wooden console designed to hold a television and hide electronics.
Features sliding doors, open shelving for media, and cable pass-through holes in the back.
Sturdy, decorative piece that anchors a living room and organizes AV equipment.

name: Modern Flat-screen TV (LED)
descriptions: Slim LED flat-screen TV on a small pedestal stand; minimalist black bezel.
Designed for mounting or placement on a low media surface; good for contemporary rooms.
Lightweight compared to older sets but typically considered a fixed display item in a bundle.

name: Modular Media Unit
descriptions: Stackable-looking modular shelving unit made for media racks and consoles.
Includes adjustable shelves, compartments for consoles and disc storage, and a cable-management slot.
Flexible arrangement for small or large living spaces; intended as a permanent fixture.

name: Vintage Stereo Cabinet
descriptions: Tall wooden cabinet built to house a turntable, receiver, and record storage.
Often has cloth-covered speaker grilles and hinged doors to protect equipment.
Adds a classic, tactile element to an entertainment bundle and conceals wiring.

name: Floor-standing Speaker Pair
descriptions: A matched pair of tall speakers meant to sit on the floor beside a TV or console.
Wooden cabinets with cloth or metal grilles and connector terminals at the rear.
Considered part of the room's fixed audio setup and packaged with entertainment furniture.
